review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. Florida Museum and species ecology sources support shallow estuarine habitat and broad temperature context; the SST band is not a calibrated preference curve.

profile.size: Min limit 36 inches TL / Bag limit 3 per harvester / day
profile.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, squids, and pelagic prey
profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for leopard shark.
factors.value_notes: Animal Diversity Web summarizes leopard sharks in shallow California bays/estuaries with reported habitat temperatures around 13-16 °C. This is habitat occurrence, not a measured preferred SST curve or a universal range across seasons and offshore movements. It supports thermal relevance but does not validate the configured 12-21 °C range or 14-19 °C ideal as a catch-response curve.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for leopard shark.
factors.value_notes: Florida Museum and Aquarium of the Pacific describe leopard sharks using sandy/muddy bays and estuaries, commonly in shallow subtidal water; Animal Diversity Web reports typical depths around 4-20 m and records to about 91 m. This supports the 1-30 m outer band and 3-25 m ideal as shallow-habitat context, not a measured universal depth-preference curve.

text.day: Full daylight when Pacific gamefish actively hunt.
